approach: The earlier job's drain fix-request work is not in this base (the previous round's Grep found no `finding_marker`, `source_fix_request` or `citing_request` in crates/), so the producer builds it. (1) pin.rs: `SourceReport` gains `findings: Vec<SourceFinding>` (study, file, kind, statement, evidence), filled from the checker's problems next to the existing `problems` strings, which stay unchanged. (2) steward.rs: add `SOURCE_FIX_MARKER`, `finding_marker`, `source_fix_request` (built only through `StewardRequest::new`) and `citing_request`. The marker is `Source fix: studies/<study>/<file> <kind> <anchor>`. The anchor is the claim id named in the statement, else the first cited path and lines in the evidence, else a short hash of the whitespace-normalised statement. So the same contradiction is skipped while its request is open, and a different one in the same file is queued. (3) drain.rs `RealSteps::check_page`: after the source check, queue one request per finding that has no open request, through `Athena::queue`. Check pass/fail and `Check::detail` are unchanged. The `study_text` doc comment stays directly above `pub fn study_text`. (4) claims.json c45: re-cite from the pinned bin/fm-teardown.sh if it can be read; otherwise re-cite at quotes already validated in the file, and the CHANGELOG says what was not read. (5) model.json and intro.json are verified by Grep and edited only if a leftover is found. (6) The passing-path drain test also asserts that no request is queued when the checker reports no problem, so criterion 3 has a concrete failure mode. (7) CHANGELOG entry.

decisions.choice: Make the marker unique per contradiction: file + kind + anchor (claim id, else cited path and lines, else statement hash), and match open requests on the whole first line.
decisions.reason: This answers the earlier duplicate-key finding. A marker of file and kind alone would skip a second, different contradiction in the same file. The claim id is the most stable thing the checker names across runs; the path-and-lines and hash fallbacks keep the key defined when no id is named.

rejected.why: A new contradiction in the same file would never be queued.

rejected.option: Key on the full statement text
rejected.why: The model rewords statements between runs, so the same contradiction would be queued again.

decisions.choice: Queue through `Athena::queue` with text from `StewardRequest::new`, and detect an open request by first line, as code_health.rs does with `structural_pass_open`.
decisions.reason: It is an existing writer and an existing open-check pattern (`Records::load`, `JobState::Closed`, a title that is the marker). `StewardRequest` guarantees `athena plan` finds acceptance and a file, and it rewords boundary words.

rejected.option: A new record type or records file for fix requests
rejected.why: It would need check_record_file/AnyRecord changes and is more than the goal needs.

rejected.option: Add a method to the `Steps` trait
rejected.why: About ten test impls of `Steps` would change. The queueing sits inside `RealSteps::check_page`, which is the real step.

decisions.choice: Keep `SourceReport.problems` as it is and add `findings` beside it.
decisions.reason: The held-back text and the existing assertions (`check.detail` contains the statement and `demo/<file>`) depend on the problem strings.

rejected.option: Parse the problem strings back into fields
rejected.why: Brittle; the structured data is already in hand where the strings are formatted.

decisions.choice: For c45, cite only quotes that are present in the cited lines, and say in the CHANGELOG what was not read.
decisions.reason: The brief allows this when the pinned source is absent. An invented line number or an unmatched quote is the earlier job's major finding.

risks.risk: Existing drain tests that run the real check over a repository now also get request records committed, which could break assertions on commit counts, `git log` or `Records` in tests/drain.rs.
risks.mitigation: The commit happens only when the fake checker reports a problem, and the changed path is limited to RealSteps::check_page. `cargo test -p athena-cli` (criteria 4 and 6) is the check, and any test that counts requests is updated in tests/drain.rs, which is a deliverable.

risks.risk: The checker words the same contradiction differently on a later run and names no claim id, so the anchor falls back to cited lines or the statement hash and a duplicate is queued.
risks.mitigation: The claim id comes first. The studies' claims all have ids and the checker is already told to quote the statement. The cost of a miss is one extra open request, not a wrong pass.

risks.risk: Queueing a request from the evidence text may fail (banned word in a path, or a multi-line statement), which would otherwise abort the check.
risks.mitigation: `StewardRequest::new` rewords boundary words and the body is built from single-line, whitespace-collapsed text; a build or queue error is appended to the check detail and never changes pass or fail.

risks.risk: c45 re-cited at lines that do not literally say 'Queued' would leave the source check unable to confirm the Queued return.
risks.mitigation: The CHANGELOG states what was not checked. The drain's source check against the real pin remains the check, and its finding would now be queued once.

risks.risk: The model-backed source check against the real pin cannot be run in this environment, so criterion 3's 'drain source check passes' is shown only with the fake checker.
risks.mitigation: The CHANGELOG states that the real-pin check was not run. The site build and conventions test cover the study's form, and the extended passing-path drain test covers the drain's passing path.

demonstrations.method: Plan step 6 adds to crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs a test named like `a_source_contradiction_queues_one_fix_request_and_is_not_queued_again_while_open`. It uses `Fixture::new()` and `commit_study` (both exist) and `RealSteps { athena, ui: &Quiet, page: &StubPage, lander }` as in `real_check` (~6857). The fake checker is injected as `Scenario.source_check = Some(Arc::new(closure))`, routed for a `# Source check` verifier call. The closure counts calls and returns: call 1 one `contradicted` problem naming claim c45 in claims.json with evidence `pinned-source/bin/fm-teardown.sh lines 30-33`; call 2 the same problem; call 3 that problem plus another naming c46 in the same file. The test calls the production `RealSteps::check_page()` three times and loads `Records::load` at head after each. It checks the queued request's text (`Source fix:` title, statement, evidence, `Acceptance:`, `Files: studies/demo/claims.json`), that `athena_core::steward::citing_request` returns it, and that the `Check` is still failed with its detail unchanged. Core unit tests in steward.rs (using the `Records::default()` fixture pattern ~2320, including a closed job) cover `finding_marker`, `source_fix_request` and `citing_request`. A pin.rs unit test covers `findings`. The refusal corpus does not cover StewardRequest, and this anchor parse is not a reading refusal rule, so no corpus case is added.
